q1_issues.issue: The scale `maturity` appears nowhere in "The benchmark 10-year note" — it is world knowledge, and no word in the sentence puts that dimension there.
The unit `point` is likewise unstated (the text says only "down 17/32"), and `down` is used as a measure scale though it names no dimension.
`(Fraction 17 32)` sits in the Measure magnitude slot, but `Fraction` is licensed as a `ProportionOf` level and the magnitude slot takes a native number or a `ParticleFromNormal` distribution.

"benchmark" is a noun modifier, which the compound rule keeps inside the fused symbol (`benchmark_note` plus genus `note`) and never predicates of the referent; the two-atom split is reserved for incidental adjectives.
The yield measure carries no `Past` wrapper although it belongs to the same past-tense clause as the `down` measure, which does.

q2_gaps: Attributive measure modifier with no stated dimension word ("10-year note"): `Measure` requires a surface scale (adjective or dimension noun), and the compound rules give no route for a numeric modifier.
Financial price-change notation "down 17/32" (32nds of a point) — no licensed form for a bare fraction change whose unit is implicit.
Vague temporal adverb "recently" — neither a calendar term nor one of the speech-anchored deictic constants, so it has no slot and is dropped.
Result infinitive "to yield 4.067 percent" hanging off a stative measure predication rather than an event — `To` needs an eventuality in its first argument.
notes: The `(Past (Measure …))` tense wrapping and the `yield` / `percent` scale-and-unit reading of "to yield 4.067 percent" follow the measure rules; the invented `maturity` and `point` symbols are the main faithfulness problem.
